Why does your voice sound so strange on a recording?

Kevin Trudeau explains that other people hear your voice entirely through their eardrums. When you speak, most of the tone you hear travels up through your skull instead.

He says only about 20% reaches your own eardrum, while 70 to 80% vibrates through bone, so the whole brain vibrates. That is why you sound different to yourself.

When did you last hear your own voice played back?
